rebuttal_or_critique: I must express my strong disagreement with the shift toward a neutral stance proposed by Dr. Goyal and Prof. Varma. While core inflation has moderated to 4.10%, headline CPI at 5.55% remains uncomfortably close to the upper tolerance limit of 6.00%. The persistence of food inflation at 8.70%, compounded by a 6.0% monsoon deficit, indicates that supply-side shocks are far from transitory. With a positive output gap of 0.60%, the economy is operating above its potential, which risks embedding inflation expectations. To pivot to a neutral stance now would be premature and could signal a premature easing of our resolve, potentially unanchoring expectations just as we are nearing the target. We must maintain the withdrawal of accommodation to ensure that the disinflationary process is durable and not derailed by these persistent food price pressures.
